summary:
Recent developments highlight ongoing advocacy efforts around D.C. statehood, with organizations pointing to federal control of the District's National Guard and budget as key concerns underscoring the need for local autonomy. A U.S. senator has committed to prioritizing D.C. statehood, while advocates continue to frame federal oversight as evidence for why the District requires full self-governance.

Without statehood, D.C. does not control its own National Guard and cannot refuse the deployment of other states' troops within its borders, and Congress can override any law the District passes or spending decisions it makes.
